newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak gas utility signs 30mln ECU loan with EIB.
newsitem.headline: Slovak gas utility signs 30mln ECU loan with EIB.

text.p: Slovak state-owned monopoly gas distributor Slovensky Plynarensky Priemysel (SPP) s.p. on Thursday signed a 30 million ECU loan with the European Investment Bank (EIB), a senior company official said.
SPP Finance Director Jan Jurga told Reuters that the credit will have maturity of 12 years, with the possibility of a two-year postponement of repayments.
Funds from the loan will be used to finance part of SPP's programme of reconstruction and developmnent of its gas distribution network.

SPP posted a 1995 net profit of around 6.5 billion crowns, most of which came from the natural gas pipeline that crosses Slovakia en route from Russia to western Europe, through which a total 80 billion cubic metres flowed last year.
Overall volume of gas transported through Slovakia from Russia is expected to increase to 92 billion cubic metres by the year 2000.
The pipeline, which began operation in 1971, now serves 10 consumers in central and western Europe.
Last week the EIB signed a 15-year, 70 million ECU loan for the Slovak state monopoly electricity utility, Slovenske Elektrarne a.s. (SE), to help finance the refurbishment of power plant at Vojany.
The credit is expected to be followed by another 65 million ECU tranche from the EIB for the same project, planned for the period 1999 to 2002.
